counting.source: Final production build, fresh Chromium context on this headless Windows host.
counting.policy: Elapsed-time curve with bounded four-point catch-up after delayed callbacks.

repeatedOpenings.contexts: Three fresh contexts plus two same-page reloads, with external fixture routing.
repeatedOpenings.notes: Five full Spidey and Dither checks passed before final clock-policy refinement. The final elapsed-time policy was then verified with a fresh Chromium opening and a WebKit opening; both completed the real Spidey animation.

preloader.communityLogo: Same hackshastra.logo URL as the existing portfolio
preloader.navigation: Internal navigation, Back and Forward remained in the same document without replaying the preloader

resolvedFindings: Covered hero images are now included in critical readiness despite inherited visibility hiding.
Completion event duplication was corrected; repeated and stalled loads emitted one completion and released locks.
Early scene preparation and controller handshaking resolved intermittent Chromium intro skips.
Dither initialization and resume now follow preloader completion and were verified with actual canvas pixels.
The noncritical-image test was corrected to release the newly critical community logo; readiness settled in 110 ms under reduced motion.
An earlier total-time assertion used the old shorter scene-preparation budget; the harness now reflects the expanded bounded preparation window.
The per-callback single-point rule could not finish on slow Windows WebKit. Elapsed-time progression with bounded catch-up now reaches 100 and completes the full Spidey animation there.
limitations: Cloudinary and Unsplash image bytes were deterministic SVG fixtures. The exact shared logo source URL and real local personal icon were checked; live remote image availability was not validated.

Windows headless WebKit functional behavior passed, including the complete Spidey animation, but its callback and rendering cadence was much slower than Chromium. This is not a three-second counting-performance or physical Safari-device claim.
WebKit screenshot capture timed out waiting for all document fonts; final WebKit verification used DOM geometry and lifecycle evidence without screenshots.
Firefox failed to launch before visiting the app. The reusable harness now uses a 30-second browser-launch limit.
Headless host timing and pixel checks do not establish physical-device frame rates. External fixture routing also does not establish HTTP-cache warm-load performance.
